Definition: to stop up; by implication, to repair; figuratively, to keep secret
BiblicalUsage: çâtham covers to stop up, to repair, to keep secret, and the Bible uses it the way ordinary people would. You find it 14 times, in 2 Chronicles among other places, and each time it is doing the same steady work. It is a word you understand best by watching where it goes, not by guessing at it.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: to stop up, to repair, to keep secret is part of how God speaks to us, and çâtham is the word He chose for it. That is reason enough to learn it.
